summary:
Radar for 2026-11-14 (GLP-1 focus). Six things stand out.

1. **Stopping and keeping results is the strongest broad long-form topic.** Coverage this week came from Medscape, Fox News, Yahoo Health ("I hit my goal weight, what now?") and Medical Daily (an unreviewed regain analysis). It also matches our proven Stopping video (7.78% CTR).
2. **"Tirzepatide not working?" is a new broad search-demand angle.** It's backed by a Nature paper (11–13 Nov) reporting that rare GLP1R variants reduce weight loss on semaglutide but not on tirzepatide, and by a real-world tirzepatide response cohort (Diabetes Metab, 12 Nov). I could not open the new Nature paper itself; my searches surfaced only the separate April 2026 23andMe Nature study.
3. **The FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning is peaking.** Fortune, The Hill, the AAO, MedPage, NeurologyLive and local TV are all covering it. It's only worth a label-change explainer that leads with the absolute risk and the symptoms that need same-day care.
4. **Psychiatric symptoms after stopping tirzepatide (NY Post, NewsNation) are moving fast in mainstream news.** The evidence is only 2 case reports, so this is a careful "what's confirmed?" Short with the scoped don't-stop line, never a scare piece.
5. **Seasonal:** Thanksgiving fullness Shorts start 11-18 (peak 11-24 to 11-27). Alcohol at holiday parties and flu-season sick-day dehydration are ready to go.
6. **Head-to-head watch:** full REDEFINE 4 results (CagriSema vs tirzepatide) at ObesityWeek 14–17 Nov. Make the fast-turn L2 only if a full randomized paper or new data comes out within 48 h; the topline is from February.

Search-demand formats included as the brief requires: a pen how-to and injection sites (IFU only), a what-to-expect timeline, the label change (NAION), felt symptoms (nausea, hair, heartburn), and an approved-drug head-to-head against tirzepatide (Foundayo).

Rejected: compounded or "research" peptide sourcing (Utah additive study, Rogan and retatrutide peptides, Join Luma), and DJ Khaled's Wegovy campaign (celebrity ad, semaglutide-only).

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): keeping results after stopping. SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335; +14.0% regain on placebo from week 36 to 88, placebo still 9.9% below starting weight) plus this week's regain headlines
candidates.angle: Broad Lane A long-form: 'You hit your goal. Now what?' What the randomized withdrawal trial actually shows, why results vary from person to person, and the habits linked to holding on (strength training, protein, a plan made with your prescriber). No stopping or tapering advice. Watch-next link to Side Effects.
keywords: what happens when you stop zepbound
candidates.predicted_peak: ongoing, with a news bump over 3–10 days; evergreen for months
candidates.why_now: Medscape ('Can patients stop GLP-1s without regaining?'), Fox News ('6 rebound risks'), Yahoo Health ('I hit my goal weight — what now?') and Medical Daily (unreviewed regain analysis) all ran in the last 72 h. This topic has appeared in 8 of our snapshots, and our Stopping video is the best-converting Lane A (7.78% CTR).

evidence.signal: Can Patients Stop GLP-1s Without Regaining Weight? (13 Nov)
I hit my goal weight on a GLP-1 — what now? (13 Nov)
Jan 2026 meta-analysis of 37 studies: most people returned to their starting weight within about 18 months of stopping (background context)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working? Why responses differ: Nature study (Nov 2026) finding rare GLP1R variants reduce weight loss on semaglutide but not tirzepatide, plus a real-world tirzepatide response cohort (Diabetes Metab, 12 Nov: weight response by diabetes status)
candidates.angle: A broad searched question answered with fresh science: what 'normal' weight loss looks like in the SURMOUNT trials, why people with type 2 diabetes tend to lose less, what the genetics research does and doesn't mean (there's no clinical test yet), and the questions to bring to your prescriber. No dose or switching advice.
keywords: why is zepbound not working for me
candidates.why_now: Nature published the rare-variant paper with a headline contrast (semaglutide vs tirzepatide), picked up by Bioengineer and Google News on 11–13 Nov. Health creators have barely covered it. 'Not working' is a high-volume evergreen search that this hook refreshes.

evidence.signal: Rare GLP1R variants diminish the weight loss effect of semaglutide but not of tirzepatide (13 Nov)
Real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in obesity: weight response, treatment factors and diabetes status (12 Nov)
Background: earlier 2026 genetics-of-response coverage (23andMe Nature study, n=27,885)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning: what the label change means, the absolute risk, and the vision symptoms that need same-day care
candidates.angle: Label-change explainer (a search-demand format): sudden, painless vision loss in one eye is the sign to act on; the risk is very rare; what the AAO and NANOS say; who was most affected (mostly adults 50 and over). Calm, numbers first, with the emergency line scoped and the don't-stop line after it.
candidates.why_now: In the last 72 h: Fortune ('30 million Americans'), The Hill op-ed, AAO explainers, MedPage, NeurologyLive, EyeWorld and local TV (WPTZ, NC5). Search demand is at its peak; most coverage is fear-led, so a calm absolute-risk explainer is the differentiator.

GLP-1 drugs taken by 30 million Americans now carry FDA warning for rare 'stroke of the eye' (13 Nov)
FDA Requires NAION Warning Across GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Class (13 Nov)

candidates.why_now: Seen in 10 consecutive snapshots. Our best-ever Reel was the 'full after 3 bites' clip (428 views). The playbook schedules holiday Shorts from 11-18, ahead of the 11-26 peak.

Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects (13 Nov): mainstream side-effect interest

candidates.topic: Psychiatric symptoms after stopping tirzepatide: what's confirmed? Two case reports (Primary Care Companion for CNS Disorders) behind the NY Post and NewsNation headlines
candidates.angle: 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short: the evidence is 2 case reports, which can't show cause or how common this is; what the authors call for; why mood changes on or off any medicine are worth raising with your prescriber; scoped emergency line plus the don't-stop/change line. No fear framing, no stopping or tapering advice.
candidates.why_now: Spread from NY Post (11 Nov) to NewsNation, India News Network and Health and Me (12–13 Nov). It's crossing into mainstream and social now; most posts overstate it, so a calm evidence-scope answer is the differentiator.

evidence.signal: Some GLP-1 patients suffer hallucinations, other psychotic symptoms after stopping drugs (11 Nov)
Why are patients reporting mania, hallucinations after stopping Ozempic? (13 Nov)
Summary of the 2 case reports (a 61-year-old hospitalized about 2 months after stopping tirzepatide)

Tirzepatide demand pushed Lilly to raise guidance (12 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: why it's linked to rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium), the label's sex split (women 7.1% vs men 0.5%), and what's worth checking with a clinician
candidates.angle: 08:00 'Is this normal?' Short with a new angle (the sex difference and timing, not 'will it grow back'), allowed once the Hair long-form is verified. Never repeat the long's title.

candidates.why_now: Our best Short ever was hair (1,025 views). A visible-body worry, the winning category for our Shorts (proven, n≈17).

evidence.signal: Hair loss 5.4% vs 0.9% placebo; women 7.1% vs men 0.5%

candidates.angle: Lane A item from the playbook. Frame it as 'what to know before the office party': alcohol plus slower gastric emptying, dehydration, the hypoglycaemia caveat. The Nov 3 DOM target-trial emulation goes in as 'linked to' context only.

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) vs tirzepatide: what the approved GLP-1 pill label says, plus the ATTAIN-OSA sleep apnea results (JAMA) and China's approval (12 Nov)

Name the populations; no switching advice. Sleep apnea as a chapter. Note: this is a cross-trial comparison of the two labels, not a randomized head-to-head, so never call it a trial result.
